newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem, Cardoso meeting "excellent" - Argentine min.
newsitem.headline: Menem, Cardoso meeting "excellent" - Argentine min.

text.p: - Argentina's Foreign Minister Guido di Tella said Sunday the two-day meeting between Argentina's President Carlos Menem and his Brazilian counterpart, Fernando Cardoso, had been "excellent" and that the two countries were heading for a "true strategic alliance."
"The meeting from all points of view was excellent because of the level of dialogue between the two leaders," Di Tella said, according to statements published by state news agency Telam.
"They talked about physical integration, customs controls and river transport," he said, upon arriving back from Rio de Janeiro.

Di Tella added that the Mercosur customs union grouping Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay "will not dissolve in 2005 when the Latin American Free Trade Agreement is established because Mercosur is an economic and political reality."
"There was also agreement on improving services between the two countries, purchases between the two governments and to strengthen macroeconomic policy," Di Tella said.

Turning to the recent changes to Brazil's import financing rules which caused a row within Mercosur, Di Tella said: "This issue was dealt with by (Argentina's) Economy Minister Roque Fernandez last week in Asuncion and in June we'll know of the differentiated treatment by Brazil towards the remaining Mercosur members."
